= Format policy: AsciiDoctor over Markdown
:frontmatter-claude-memory-name: AsciiDoctor over Markdown for human-consumed files
:frontmatter-claude-memory-description: The Lieutenant's 2026-05-18 format policy. AsciiDoctor (.adoc) is the canonical source for any file a human will read; Markdown (.md) is acceptable only where the Claude Code harness requires it. When a file must exist in .md form (e.g., memory files), a parallel .adoc source must also exist, and the .md is derived from the .adoc by the downdoc converter via a pre-commit hook.
:frontmatter-claude-memory-type: feedback
:frontmatter-claude-memory-origin-session-id: 4b69ca29-dc2a-4765-b3f9-9d7a0925322d

== Why

Markdown has weaker semantics than AsciiDoctor: no built-in admonitions, weaker tables, no native cross-references, and no document-header attribute mechanism for metadata.
AsciiDoctor provides all of these natively.
Authoring in AsciiDoctor and converting to Markdown only at the harness boundary preserves authorial intent and keeps the source format consistent across documents.

== When .md is allowed

* Memory files in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/*.md` — the harness's auto-memory loader requires the `.md` extension.
* README on npm-published packages — npm and yarn package registries assume Markdown.
* Any other harness or third-party tool that requires Markdown specifically.

In every such case, the `.adoc` parallel source is canonical.
The `.md` is regenerated from `.adoc` by the pre-commit hook in `~/continental/`, which invokes downdoc with `--frontmatter-vendor=claude`.

== Authoring rule

When creating any new file the Lieutenant will read directly, default to the `.adoc` extension.
When asked to produce a `.md` deliverable (and only then), produce the `.adoc` source alongside it and check both into the same repository.
The `.md` must never be hand-edited; it is a build artifact derived from the `.adoc`.
